title: Regulatory Definitions and Operational Frameworks
summary: This thread tracks the formalization of specialized customs entities such as AEOs, Express Services, and E-commerce operators. It reflects a shift toward institutionalizing specific business models within the customs regulatory framework.

evolution.institutionalization: Moved from general definitions to specific, compliance-heavy operational categories like AEO.

timeline.change: Defined specific operational categories for express and e-commerce entities.
Formalized the Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) status and institutional oversight.
Operationalized the rejection/evaluation criteria for AEO status.
Replicated definitions for express and e-commerce services.

On-board Express Service: This term refers to individuals or institutions licensed under these rules to provide express goods transport services via authorized land customs routes.
International Air Express Service: This term refers to individuals or institutions licensed under these rules to provide express goods transport services through customs airports.
Cross-Border E-commerce Institution: This refers to e-commerce entities that display goods electronically and, upon receiving supply orders, facilitate the direct delivery or supply of goods to customers across national borders using express services.
Gift Items: This is defined in accordance with the provisions specified in the prevailing Import Policy Order.
Express Service Institution: This category encompasses both On-Board Express Services and International Air Express Services.
Agent: This refers to individuals or institutions licensed under Section 243 of the Customs Act.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: The definition of this system is derived from the definition provided in Section 2(15) of the Customs Act.
Consignee: The term refers to the recipient identified in the bill of lading, house airway bill, or consignment note issued by the consignor, principal, authorized agent, or counterpart.
Documents: This includes items of no commercial value such as handwritten or printed materials, tender documents, maps, technical designs, survey reports, manuals, passports, and various publications packaged for transport.
De Minimis: This refers to the definition of de minimis value as prescribed under the Customs (De Minimis) Rules, 2019.
Samples: This refers to goods classified as genuine samples under the prevailing Import Policy Order.
Consignor: This refers to the sender identified in the bill of lading, house airway bill, or consignment note issued by the principal or their authorized agent or counterpart.
Forms: This refers to the standardized documents prescribed for use under these rules.
Advertising Materials: This is defined in accordance with the criteria set forth in the prevailing Import Policy Order.
Person: For the purposes of these rules, this definition includes companies, partnerships, limited companies, and other organizations.
Licensee: This refers to the license granted under these rules for the management and clearance of goods imported or exportable through an express service institution.
Licensing Authority: This refers to the specific authority designated for licensing purposes as defined in the rules.

Authorized Economic Operator: An Authorized Economic Operator is defined as an entity that has been granted recognition certification in accordance with the specified rules.
This is the designated regulatory agency responsible for monitoring, though other customs offices may act as monitoring agencies within their respective jurisdictions for certified entities.
Customs Act 2023: The Act is formally defined as the Customs Act 2023 (Act No. 57 of 2023).
Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Commi: The Committee refers to the specific oversight body designated in the rules for handling matters related to authorized economic operators.
Customs Officer: A Customs Officer is defined as any official appointed under Section 4 of the Customs Act 2023.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is defined as the National Board of Revenue established under the National Board of Revenue Order, 1972.
Logistics Operator: A Logistics Operator is a service provider involved in the customs process, such as a customs agent, shipping agent, freight forwarder, terminal operator, or courier service provider.
Affiliated Institution: This term encompasses businesses or companies linked to the same ownership, partnership, or directorship, including cases where individuals serve as chairmen or directors across multiple entities.
Provisional Certificate: A Provisional Certificate is a time-bound certification issued by the Committee subject to the fulfillment of specific conditions.
Recognition Certificate: A Recognition Certificate is the formal accreditation issued under the relevant rules for authorized economic operators.

(আবেদনকারীর নাম ও ঠিকানা)

Authorized Economic Operator: This form is the official notification used by the Authorized Economic Operator Center to inform an applicant that their application for status advancement has been rejected.

The rejection occurs when an applicant fails to meet specific conditions or demonstrates deficiencies during the evaluation process conducted by the Authorized Economic Operator Committee under the rules of 2024.
The document requires the inclusion of specific reasons for the rejection, such as incomplete criteria or non-compliance with established requirements.
Authorized Economic Operator (Recognitio: This rule framework provides the legal authority for the assessment and evaluation of applications submitted by companies seeking AEO status.
It outlines the procedural grounds under which the Authorized Economic Operator Committee may approve or reject applications for status advancement based on institutional deficiencies.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is the governing body responsible for issuing the rules that regulate the recognition and management of Authorized Economic Operators in Bangladesh.

On-board Express Service: An On-board Express Service is defined as a person or entity licensed under sub-rule (3) of rule 6 to provide express delivery services for goods through authorized land customs routes.
International Air Express Service: An International Air Express Service refers to a person or entity licensed under sub-rule (3) of rule 6 to provide express delivery services through customs airports.
Cross-Border E-commerce Institution: A cross-border e-commerce institution is defined as a business that displays goods via electronic means, receives orders, and supplies or delivers those goods directly to consumers across international borders using express services.
Gift Goods: Gift goods are defined in accordance with the specific criteria for genuine gift items as described in the Import Policy Order current at the time.
Express Service Provider: This term refers collectively to entities operating as either an On-board Express Service or an International Air Express Service.
Agent: An agent refers to a person or entity that holds a valid license granted under section 243 of the Customs Act.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: This term is defined by reference to the specific definition provided in section 2, clause (15) of the Customs Act.
Consignee: A consignee is identified as the recipient of goods as specified in the bill of lading, house airway bill, or consignment note issued by the Consignor, principal, or their authorized agent.
Documents: Documents encompass items with no commercial value such as printed materials, technical designs, surveys, catalogs, manuals, passports, and similar items packed in envelopes, cartons, or bundles.
De Minimis: De minimis is defined as per the criteria established in clause (a) of rule 2 of the Customs (De Minimis) Rules, 2019.
Samples: Samples are defined in accordance with the specifications provided for genuine trade samples in the relevant Import Policy Order.
Consignor: The Consignor is defined as the party listed as the sender on the bill of lading, house airway bill, or consignment note, including the principal or their authorized agent.
Forms: This term refers to the specific documents and forms prescribed for use under these rules.
Advertising Materials: Advertising material refers to items defined as genuine advertising goods according to the relevant Import Policy Order.
Person: The term person extends to include companies, partnerships, limited companies, and other legal entities.
Licensee: A license is defined as the authorization granted under rule 6 for the management and customs clearance of goods imported or exported through express service providers.
Licensing Authority: The Licensing Authority refers to the body designated with regulatory powers as described in rule 4.
